# Preliminary results (auto-generated by analyse.py)

## A. Phase 1 ground-truth test (15 objects, tape-measured; source: phase_1_local_life_testing.pdf)
Dimensions compared largest-to-largest (orientation-independent). "Envelope" = L x W x H of the real object.

| Metric | Result |
|---|---|
| Median dimension error | 7.5 % |
| Dimensions within 10 % / 20 % | 58 % / 84 % of 45 |
| Median volume error vs actual envelope | 35.0 % (only 5/15 within 25 %) |
| Material correct | 8/15 |
| Colour exact / close | 6/15 exact, +5 close (e.g. white->grey, pink->red) |

Note: reported litres are the measured (height-map) volume, not a box envelope, so volume "error" mixes shape and measurement error. Which camera produced this table must be stated in the thesis.

## B. Automatic dual-camera log (comparison_measurements.csv, 22-29 Sep, 243 rows, no ground truth)

| | RealSense | Logitech |
|---|---|---|
| Attempts | 119 | 124 |
| Accepted | 68 (57 %) | 50 (40 %) |
| Rejected with reason | 18 | 28 |
| Missing (no final reading) | 33 | 46 |
| Implausible-size outliers | 2 | 1 |
| Usable after flagging | 56 | 40 |

Paired events where both cameras accepted: 15; of these only 5 are the same object type in both cameras
(the rest were paired with a different object by the time window) -> no cross-camera accuracy claim from this log.
Top rejection reasons: RealSense [('no_valid_measurement', 8), ('unstable_volume', 5), ('candidate_spans_the_measurement_zone', 3)]; Logitech [('no_measurable_height_above_plane', 15), ('no_valid_measurement', 8), ('unstable_volume', 5)].
